StackType.issue: Closed 2026-07-30 (tier-2 campaign): (Task 25.) The 15 `on_stack` no-op overrides are DELETED; the base `Power.on_stack` adds, matching PowerCmd.ModifyAmount (PowerCmd.cs:236), which adds unconditionally with no StackType branch -- PowerStackType.Single means 'Amount is hidden and displayed as 1' (PowerStackType.cs:10-13), not 'does not stack'. All 16 units re-verified against their own C#: 15 are StackType.Single, and NONE overrides InstanceType (PowerModel.cs:144 default None), so none needs T1's instance machinery instead of amount-adding. Two per-site exceptions, both verified: (1) DAMPEN's C# StackType is actually `None`, not Single (DampenPower.cs:22) -- the queue's 16-unit list was wrong about it; its only applier, MagiKnight, dedupes caller-side (MagiKnight.cs:78-96: re-application calls AddCaster only and never reaches PowerCmd.Apply), so the deletion is inert through the real caller and T28's caster-set machinery is untouched and re-pinned. (2) HEX genuinely reads Amount (HexPower.cs:79 feeds CardCmd.Afflict<Hexed>(card, Amount)), so this deletion closes a real divergence that remains DORMANT only because SpectralKnight's move machine never loops back to HEX and KnightsElite fields exactly one -- a second Hex applier makes it live. ILLUSION needed no override and is unchanged (the opposite-sign case the record notes). No reachable re-application among the other 13: Burrowed and Soar re-apply only after their own expire/remove, always onto a fresh instance. Pins: test/test_stack_type_single.py (39 tests).  The text it replaced read: PowerStackType.Single, and the sim overrides Power.on_stack to `pass` citing it -- which is WRONG about C# and inert about this power. Single means only 'Amount is hidden, and is always 1' (PowerStackType.cs:10-13); PowerCmd.ModifyAmount:236 adds the offset with no StackType branch at all, so in the game a second application really does raise Amount to 2. This unit is one of the 15 the stack census flags (py audit/tools/power_census.py stack) and the main report's section 7 item 5 covers the class. DORMANT here for the per-unit reason the census leaves open: nothing reads this power's Amount -- not the power itself, not any sim listener, and not the C# model (whose only Amount reader is the hidden DisplayAmount). Named trigger: any future effect that scales with the stack count, or a UI that shows it. For this unit the dormancy is airtight in a second way: C#'s only Amount reader would be DisplayAmount, which ConfusedPower does not override, and the sim's on_card_drawn never consults self.amount. Both ported appliers apply exactly 1 (relics/snecko_eye.py:28, relics/fake_snecko_eye.py:22) from on_combat_start, so a second application inside one combat is not even reachable today -- but Snecko Eye and Fake Snecko Eye are both obtainable in one run, which is precisely the case that would reach it.

AfterCardDrawn.rationale: Fires on every draw for the owner, sets the drawn card's cost for the rest of the combat, and skips X-cost cards. ConfusedPower.cs:31-45 vs powers.py:3867-3873 line for line: the owner filter (:33-36, a single-player tautology the sim omits), the X-cost bail (:37-40 EnergyCost.Canonical < 0 vs :3868 card.energy_cost_x), and EnergyCost.SetThisCombat(cost) (:42 vs :3873 card.set_cost_this_combat). The `fromHandDraw` argument is read by neither side, so turn-start and mid-turn draws are both randomised. NCard.PlayRandomizeCostAnim (:43) is presentation.

guards.issue: Closed 2026-07-29 (round 6): closed by the same edit as relic/snecko_eye/g1. ConfusedPower.NextEnergyCost (ConfusedPower.cs:47-54) ends in `RunState.Rng.CombatEnergyCosts.NextInt(4)`, and powers.py's ConfusedPower.on_card_drawn now reads `combat.combat_rng.energy` -- combat_energy_costs in a parity run, the shared legacy Random in RL play. Pinned by test_combat_rng.py::test_confused_cost_draws_from_the_energy_cost_stream.  The text it replaced read: WRONG RNG STREAM. C# draws the cost from base.Owner.Player.RunState.Rng.CombatEnergyCosts; powers.py:3873 uses combat._rng.randrange(4), the SHARED unseeded random.Random (combat.py:88). combat.combat_rng.energy (combat_rng.py:23,53 -- the combat_energy_costs stream) is the matching accessor and exists. The range is right on both sides (NextInt(4) is 0..3 and randrange(4) is 0..3, so costs 0-3 inclusive, which the sim's docstring states). Same defect as power/aggression's (main report section 4 item 8) and as power/hello_world, power/entropy and power/stampede in half A, and LIVE for the same reason with an unusually wide blast radius: Confused re-costs EVERY card the player draws for the whole combat, so under seed parity a Snecko Eye run diverges on the first draw and every shared-rng consumer after it is perturbed. Both appliers are ported relics (relics/snecko_eye.py:25-28, relics/fake_snecko_eye.py:19-22), so binding rule 6 is satisfied. Third-file citations, not hashed here.

guards.rationale: A TestMode.AssertOn()-gated hook for the game's own tests (ConfusedPower.cs:25). Not gameplay; the sim has no analogue and needs none.
Neither side ticks or removes it; the re-costing lasts the combat, and SetThisCombat means already-drawn cards keep their rolled cost. Both agree.
